approach.en: Divide array into halves, recursively sort each half, then merge sorted halves using two pointers.

code.python:
def merge_sort(arr, l, r):
    if l >= r: return
    m = (l+r)//2
    merge_sort(arr, l, m)
    merge_sort(arr, m+1, r)
    L, R = arr[l:m+1], arr[m+1:r+1]
    i = j = 0; k = l
    while i < len(L) and j < len(R):
        if L[i] <= R[j]: arr[k] = L[i]; i += 1
        else: arr[k] = R[j]; j += 1
        k += 1
    while i < len(L): arr[k] = L[i]; i += 1; k += 1
    while j < len(R): arr[k] = R[j]; j += 1; k += 1

code.python:
def count_inversions(arr, l, r):
    if l >= r: return 0
    m = (l+r)//2
    inv = count_inversions(arr,l,m) + count_inversions(arr,m+1,r)
    L, R = arr[l:m+1], arr[m+1:r+1]
    i = j = 0; k = l
    while i < len(L) and j < len(R):
        if L[i] <= R[j]: arr[k]=L[i]; i+=1
        else: arr[k]=R[j]; j+=1; inv+=len(L)-i
        k+=1
    while i<len(L): arr[k]=L[i]; i+=1; k+=1
    while j<len(R): arr[k]=R[j]; j+=1; k+=1
    return inv

code.python:
def my_pow(x, n):
    if n == 0: return 1.0
    if n < 0: x = 1/x; n = -n
    half = my_pow(x, n//2)
    if n % 2 == 0: return half * half
    return x * half * half

problems.title: Karatsuba Multiplication

description.en: Implement the Karatsuba algorithm for multiplying two large numbers. The Karatsuba algorithm uses the Divide and Conquer approach to multiply two n-digit numbers in O(n^1.585) time, faster than the naive O(n^2) method. Given two non-negative integers represented as strings, return their product as a string.
description.hi: Do bade numbers ko multiply karne ke liye Karatsuba algorithm implement karo. Karatsuba algorithm Divide and Conquer approach use karke do n-digit numbers ko O(n^1.585) time mein multiply karta hai, jo naive O(n^2) method se tez hai. Do non-negative integers strings ke roop mein diye hain, unka product string mein return karo.

constraints: num1 and num2 contain only digits
No leading zeros except the number 0 itself

hints.en: Split each number into two halves: high and low digits
hints.hi: Har number ko do halves mein split karo: high aur low digits

hints.en: For x = xH * 10^m + xL and y = yH * 10^m + yL, compute three products instead of four: z0 = xL*yL, z2 = xH*yH, z1 = (xH+xL)*(yH+yL) - z2 - z0
hints.hi: x = xH * 10^m + xL aur y = yH * 10^m + yL ke liye, chaar ki jagah teen products compute karo: z0 = xL*yL, z2 = xH*yH, z1 = (xH+xL)*(yH+yL) - z2 - z0

starterCode.python:

num2 = input().strip()
print(karatsuba(num1, num2))

approach.en: Split numbers into halves. Compute 3 products instead of 4: z0=low*low, z2=high*high, z1=(high+low)*(high+low)-z2-z0. Combine: z2*10^(2m) + z1*10^m + z0.
approach.hi: Numbers ko halves mein split karo. 4 ki jagah 3 products compute karo: z0=low*low, z2=high*high, z1=(high+low)*(high+low)-z2-z0. Combine: z2*10^(2m) + z1*10^m + z0.

code.python:
def karatsuba(x, y):
    if x < 10 or y < 10: return x * y
    n = max(len(str(x)), len(str(y)))
    m = n // 2
    p = 10 ** m
    xH, xL = x // p, x % p
    yH, yL = y // p, y % p
    z0 = karatsuba(xL, yL)
    z2 = karatsuba(xH, yH)
    z1 = karatsuba(xH + xL, yH + yL) - z2 - z0
    return z2 * (10 ** (2*m)) + z1 * (10 ** m) + z0
